prompt_text: I need a personal injury attorney in Chicago after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry you’re dealing with this — here are several Chicago personal-injury firms you should call and why each is worth contacting. I can’t guarantee results; check recent reviews and confirm details when you call.

Top firms to call
- Clifford Law Offices (Chicago) — long-standing, high-profile personal-injury and wrongful-death firm with extensive trial experience and many large verdicts/settlements in catastrophic car-accident cases. Good if injuries are severe or complex.
- Corboy & Demetrio — one of Chicago’s most recognized plaintiff trial firms; strong track record in auto collisions, catastrophic injuries and wrongful-death litigation.
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard P.C. — boutique-ish trial-focused personal-injury firm known for aggressive representation and strong settlements/verdicts in motor-vehicle matters.
- Power Rogers (Power Rogers, LLC/Power Rogers & Smith) — focuses on auto, truck and catastrophic-accident cases; known locally for client-focused representation of crash victims.
- The Cochran Firm Chicago — national brand with local Chicago trial attorneys who handle car crashes and catastrophic personal-injury claims.
- Rosenfeld Injury Lawyers, LLC — plaintiff-focused firm that handles car and truck accident claims statewide, often consumer-facing (free consults, case resources for crash victims).

Why these (brief)
- Trial experience: they will take cases past settlement when necessary, which often yields better results.
- Specialization: these firms focus on plaintiff-side car/truck accidents and catastrophic injuries rather than general practice or insurance defense.
- Resources: larger firms can hire accident reconstructionists, medical experts and investigators you may need.
- Free consults/contingency: most offer free initial consultations and work on contingency (no fee unless they recover money), but always confirm the fee/cost policy.

What to ask on the first call
- Do you take cases like mine (car vs. car, rear-end, T-bone, truck, uninsured motorist)? Experience with injuries like mine?
- Do you handle cases on contingency? Percentage and who pays out-of-pocket costs if we lose?
- Who in the firm will handle the file (partner/associate/paralegal), and how will I communicate with them?
- Do you have trial experience in cases like this? Any recent outcomes I can review?
- Expected timeline and what evidence you’ll need from me.
- Will you advance medical or expert costs?

Documents and info to have ready when you call
- Police report number and officer contact (if any)
- Photos of the scene, vehicle damage, visible injuries
- Names/contacts for other driver(s) and witnesses
- Insurance info (yours and others’)
- Medical records or bills, even initial ER notes
- Dates you missed work and pay stubs (if lost wages)

Immediate next steps (if you haven’t already)
- Seek medical care and preserve medical records
- Take photos of injuries and vehicle damage
- Get the police report
- Do not give recorded statements to insurers without counsel
- Save receipts/records for all accident-related expenses

How to pick among them
- Arrange free consultations (you can and should call 3–4). Pay attention to responsiveness, clarity about fees, and whether the lawyer has specific experience with your crash type and injury severity.
- Check recent client reviews, AVVO/Martindale-Hubbell ratings, and any reported verdicts/settlements.

If you want, tell me:
- The date/type of crash, injuries, and whether the police or insurance companies are already involved — I can suggest which of these firms might be the best to call first and draft a short script you can use on the call.
